title: Sell Mineral Rights in Farmington, WV
metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Farmington, WV | Marion County
metaDescription: Farmington, WV mineral owner in Marion County coal country? We buy gas and oil mineral interests separate from any coal estate, title-checked first.
heroLead: Farmington's name is tied to coal in most people's minds, but the mineral tracts around this small Marion County town carry a gas leasing history that runs parallel to, and separate from, the coal that made the town known.
intro: Coal companies acquired the coal seam under much of Farmington-area land decades ago, in some cases reserving it entirely apart from the oil and gas rights, which frequently stayed with the surface-owning family or were leased independently. That separation is the starting point for evaluating any Farmington mineral interest.
We buy oil and gas mineral and royalty interests around Farmington directly, confirming which estate your family actually holds before we make an offer.

sections.heading: Coal reservations and the gas estate left behind
paragraphs: A Farmington-area deed that reserved coal to a mining company decades ago typically left oil and gas rights untouched. We trace that specific reservation to confirm what remains available to buy, since assuming the whole mineral estate transferred with the coal is a common and costly mistake.

sections.heading: Gas leasing continuing quietly alongside coal history
paragraphs: Marion County has seen ongoing gas leasing activity even in towns whose identity is centered on coal. A Farmington-area gas interest can be active and producing independent of whatever happened with the coal seam beneath it, and a family that only ever heard about the coal lease can still be owed a gas royalty.

That independence between the two estates is worth remembering if the only paperwork your family kept was the coal lease. The gas rights may have followed an entirely different path through the same generations.

sections.heading: Family ownership across generations
paragraphs: Farmington's mineral interests, like much of Marion County, have typically split among heirs over multiple generations without formal partition. We identify the current record owners through the deed and probate history before pricing an interest.

faqs.question: The coal company owns the coal under our old family land. Do they also own the gas?
faqs.answer: Not necessarily. Coal and gas are frequently separate estates in Marion County. We check the specific reservation language for your tract.

faqs.question: Is there still gas leasing activity in the Farmington area?
faqs.answer: Yes, though it varies by tract. We check current lease and unit status before evaluating your interest.

faqs.question: How do I find my family's mineral interest if the paperwork was lost?
faqs.answer: We can search the Marion County deed record using your family name and the general tract location to reconstruct the chain of title.
